To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
it is possible, using Quest, to estimate the number and type of acquisitions needed to acquire a quantifiable spectrum from acquisitions without water-suppression in brain tumor patients.
it is possible for the physician to estimate the number acquisitions needed to obtain an MRS quantifiable spectrum in brain tumors, before its acquisition.
it is possible, by using the Quest software, to estimate the number and type of acquisitions needed to guarantee quantification of a tumor spectrum.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the optimization of brain tumor MRS acquisition, which is of great importance for the comparison of different studies.
the optimization of MRS brain tumors acquisition time in order to obtain quantifiable spectra for comparison with other spectra.
the optimization of MRS acquisition time, in order to obtain spectra which can be compared between studies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the number of acquisitions to obtain a quantified spectrum is not the same for all brain tumors, and it is necessary to use a quantitative method in order to obtain a quantification.
it is possible, using Quest and Amares, to estimate the number and type of acquisitions that are needed to obtain a spectrum that can be quantified.
it is possible, with the use of a quantitative tool, to estimate the number acquisitions needed to obtain quantifiable spectra, and thus, optimize acquisition time.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we can use Quest and Amares in order to predict the number of acquisitions that would be needed for the tumor spectra to be quantifiable, thus allowing us to save time and resources.
the Quest method is more robust for brain tumors than Amares and can be used in clinical routine to predict whether or not a spectrum will be quantified.
it is possible, by using Quest, to estimate the number and duration of acquisitions needed to guarantee a quantifiable tumor spectrum before its acquisition.

, for a given voxel, the number of acquisitions necessary to obtain a quantified spectrum is independent of the voxel position and the presence of blood residue or metal.
